headline: ...REMNANTS OF RACHEL BRINGING HEAVY RAINS AND GUSTY WINDS TO PORTIONS OF THE SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES... ...THIS IS THE LAST NHC ADVISORY ON THIS SYSTEM...

sections.text: LOCATION...35.8N 114.6W ABOUT 255 MI...415 KM NNE OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 15 DEGREES AT 29 MPH...46 KM/H MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
sections.title: SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION

sections.text:
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

The government of Mexico has discontinued all coastal warnings.

SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:

There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.

For more information, Please consult products from your local weather office.
sections.title: WATCHES AND WARNINGS

sections.text:
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the remnants of Rachel were located near latitude 35.8 North, longitude 114.6 West. The remnants are moving toward the north-northeast near 29 mph (46 km/h).

Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.

The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
sections.title: DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK

sections.text:
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.

WIND: High Wind Warnings and Wind Advisories are in effect across the southwestern United States. Gusty winds associated with the remnants of Rachel are spreading over interior portions of the southwestern United States, especially in areas of higher terrain, today and tomorrow. For more information, Please consult products from your local weather office.

RAINFALL: Rachel and its associated moisture will bring total rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5 inches from Southern California into the Great Basin and portions of the Southwest United States through today. This will continue to lead to the potential for significant flash and urban flooding.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.

SURF: Waves generated by Rachel will continue along the coasts of Southern California and northern Baja California today. These waves, combined with an incoming long-period southerly swell, will cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Coastal flooding and erosion are expected to worsen this morning as the highest waves coincide with the high tides and water levels that are already running well above predicted levels. Moderate to major coastal flooding is expected, with hazardous coastal conditions continuing the next few days. Please consult products from your local weather office.
sections.title: HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND

sections.text:
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane Center on this system. For more information, Please consult products from your local weather office at https://www.weather.gov/

Rainfall forecasts for the United States can always be found at https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/qpf2.shtml and outlooks of flash flood risks can be found at https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/excessive_rainfall_outlook_ero.php .
